environment.description: Same Django 4.2 application deployed on EC2 with PostgreSQL 15 RDS instance. The database connection is configured through RDS Proxy using IAM authentication. The PostgreSQL role 'webapp_readonly' used by the application was provisioned via a Terraform module that applies principle-of-least-privilege grants. The role has column-level SELECT on profile_comments(author, comment_text, created_at, profile_id) and row-level SELECT on auth_user. No DML mutation privileges were granted; the pg_hba.conf on the RDS parameter group enforces the role mapping. Application also sits behind nginx with proxy_pass but no additional filtering middleware.

config.database: PostgreSQL 15 on RDS with RDS Proxy (IAM auth)
config.db_grants: GRANT SELECT (author, comment_text, created_at, profile_id) ON profile_comments TO webapp_readonly; -- No INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE granted
config.notes: The application code is identical; INSERT/UPDATE statements will raise psycopg2.errors.InsufficientPrivilege at runtime
